dedupe_keys.name: wayside energy storage for regenerative braking energy in the new york city subway con edison white paper

description: This white paper by Ahmed Mohamed of CUNY City College, Andrew Reid of Con Edison and Thomas Lamb of New York City Transit (NYCT), published by Consolidated Edison, summarises a joint study of wayside energy storage systems (ESS) that recover regenerative braking energy in the NYCT subway, which uses more than 1,600 GWh of electricity a year. Coverage: a four-week experiment that disabled regenerative braking on all trains on the 7 Line and compared substation energy and power; metering of trains on the 7 Line giving 11 datasets of speed, third rail voltage, current and power; and a high-fidelity physics-based transient model, validated against measurements, used to size ESS and set functional requirements, with a benefit-cost framework. A train draws about 15 to 20 kWh when accelerating with a peak near 4 MW, and 7 Line rectifier substations peak twice a weekday at about 25 MW. Format and access: a 21-page PDF. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: one line, and the paper is undated on the pages read. The findings (about 8% savings today, about 35% with wayside ESS; flywheels and supercapacitors viable) can size traction storage in rail power capacity planning and optimisation models. It relates to MTA open data and the ELECTRA traction substation dataset in the catalogue.

name: Wayside energy storage for regenerative braking energy in the New York City subway (Con Edison white paper)
outcomes: Existing regenerative braking cuts 7 Line substation energy and peak demand by about 8% over 24 hours; wayside energy storage could raise savings to about 35%; flywheels and supercapacitors are viable fast-response technologies.
provider: Ahmed Mohamed (CUNY City College), Andrew Reid (Con Edison) and Thomas Lamb (New York City Transit), published by Consolidated Edison Company of New York
